Multiplicity

mul-tih-PLIS-ih-tee -- from Latin multi- ('many') + plicare ('to fold'). · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Multiplicity is a large number and variety of different things.

The conference schedule offered a multiplicity of workshops, so no two attendees ended up with the same day.

Worked Example

Instead of one single design, the architects presented a multiplicity of possible layouts, from a compact studio to a sprawling open floor plan.

That sheer number of different options, all available at once, is exactly what multiplicity describes.

How Multiplicity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

variety

variety: a number of different types

abundance

abundance: a very large quantity of something

Antonyms

scarcity

scarcity: a very small, insufficient supply

uniformity

uniformity: the quality of being all the same

How Strong Is It? — variety → multiplicity → abundance

variety vs. multiplicity

variety vs. multiplicity: Variety is weaker than multiplicity: a cafeteria's variety means a decent range of side dishes, while a multiplicity is a far larger, almost overwhelming number of different options.

abundance vs. multiplicity

abundance vs. multiplicity: Abundance is stronger than multiplicity: a multiplicity of wildflowers means many kinds growing at once, while an abundance goes further — the valley overflows with them after record rainfall.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — multi-

prefix — multi-: many (Latin)

root — -plic-

root — -plic-: to fold (Latin (plicare))

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state or quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Multiplicity combines multi- ('many') with plicare ('to fold') and -ity ('state or quality of') -- the same folding imagery behind multiply and duplicate, so a multiplicity is the state of having many 'folds,' many versions or varieties at once.
